entry.rationale: Purple acid phosphatase performs metal-assisted phosphate ester hydrolysis, fitting the metal-dependent hydrolase seed.

mechanism_evidence.fit: Metal-bound phosphate ester hydrolysis with Fe(III)-bound hydroxide in-line attack matches metal_dependent_hydrolase.
mechanism_evidence.mechanism_text: On the basis of structural studies with bound phosphate and tungstate (inhibitor), and the observed inversion of the phosphorous configuration during catalysis, an SN2-type mechanism is proposed for PAP. The substrate phosphate is bound to the Me(II) ion via one of the non-esterified oxygen atoms and oriented by His202 and His296 (numbering for kidney bean enzyme) for in-line attack of an Fe(III)-bound hydroxide ion from a position opposite the esterified oxygen. These residues and the metal ions are presumed to stabilise the pentaco-ordinate transition state. Tentatively, His296 may then act as a general acid to protonate the leaving group, followed by the attack of a water molecule on the Fe(III) atom to release the inorganic phosphate.
